c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: The two silver circles at the front of the car are not eyes. What are they?

B.text: A sound sender and a sound listener

c1.why: One sends out a sound too high to hear; the other listens for the echo. Timing that echo is how the distance comes out.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: `HC-SR04 Sonar unit Centimeters` gives you what?

C.text: Yes or no — something is there

c2.why: It is a measurement. What counts as "too close" is a decision you make about that number.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: Why does the test check `Sonar > 1` as well as `Sonar < 20`?

A.text: Because the very smallest readings are not trustworthy

B.text: Because 1 is the smallest number allowed

D.text: To make the car turn twice

c3.why: The sensor has a floor. Very small readings are noise, so the test needs a bottom end as well as a top.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: A wall is 40cm ahead. What does the car do?
r1.why: 40 is outside the band, so the test is false and the `else` branch runs.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: A box is 12cm ahead. What do the wheels do?

B.text: The left stops and the right reverses, so the car swings aside

r2.why: `0, -50` is one wheel still and the other backing up — that pivots the car away from what is in front of it.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: The reading is taken outside the loop. What goes wrong?

B.text: The car uses the same measurement forever

r3.why: One reading, taken at start-up, is used for every decision after that. The car is deciding about a room it saw once.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: There is no `else`. What does the car do in open space?

B.text: Keeps doing whatever it was last told

r4.why: With no `else` branch, nothing new is sent to the motors — so they hold their last instruction.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: In an empty room this car sometimes swerves for no reason. Which change fixes it?

B.text: Take the reading outside the loop

d1.why: A stray reading of 0 or 1 passes `< 20` and looks like an obstacle. The bottom end of the range throws those out.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: This car drives straight into every wall. What is missing?

B.text: The block that reads the sonar into the variable

d2.why: The variable is never filled, so it stays at 0 — which fails the test, so the car drives on forever.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Put the loop in order: 1 turn away or drive on · 2 read the sonar into a variable · 3 test whether the reading is in the danger band
b1.why: Measure, decide, act — every trip round the loop, in that order.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: Which test means "closer than 20cm, and close enough to be real"?
b2.why: `and` is what makes a band. Both ends have to be true at the same time for the reading to count.
